investigations.name: glucose-regulation
investigations.title: Glucose Regulation — COPASI vs Tellurium
investigations.question:
For BioModels matching "glucose regulation", do COPASI and Tellurium agree on
the time-course dynamics — and which models diverge or fail to load in one engine?
investigations.hypothesis:
Most curated glucose-regulation SBML models integrate to near-identical
trajectories under COPASI and Tellurium; disagreements flag either engine-
specific loading issues or genuinely stiff/edge-case models worth follow-up.
Confirmed: a live 5-model run found the one curated `BIOMD*` model that
loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633, Bulik2016 hepatic glucose
metabolism) agrees near-perfectly (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, "Good"),
cross-validated by the committed full-corpus dataset's independent
measurement of the same model (1.61e-07, also "good"). The other 4/5 —
all non-curated `MODEL*` preprint entries — failed identically on a
missing SED-ML file, an engine-agnostic loading gap rather than a
disagreement.

investigations.name: hra-3d
investigations.title: HRA-3D — Model Coverage on the Human Reference Atlas 3D Anatomy
investigations.question:
Which of the HRA's 1,730 Uberon-keyed anatomical structures (2,295 raw
ASCT+B-3D crosswalk rows, 114 source-organ GLBs) are covered by a
mechanistic model — at a single query's scale and at the full
1,096-model curated-corpus scale — and can we view that coverage/linkage
directly on the 3D anatomy?
investigations.hypothesis:
The full ASCT+B-3D anatomical-structure crosswalk (2,295 rows, 1,730 with
a resolvable Uberon CURIE, below the ~81 per-organ reference-organ GLBs)
and a sub-organ-scale FTU digital object (glomerulus) are both loadable
via thin Steps; crossing the crosswalk with the hra-integration
investigation's biomodel-DO organ->models index (at organ granularity) is
enough to mark model coverage over anatomical structures/organs and to
join each covered model to the exact GLB scene node it maps to — giving a
coverage/linkage layer that a three.js viewer can render directly on a
reference-organ 3D model, without a heavyweight per-AS-node
model-matching pipeline. Confirmed: a single 25-result query covers only
58/1,730 AS nodes (liver + pancreas), while crossing the full curated
1,096-model corpus covers 635/1,730 (31/114 organs) — an order of
magnitude wider, and wide enough to newly reach kidney.

investigations.name: hra-integration
investigations.title: HRA API Integration — Datasets, Ontology, and BioModel Digital Objects
investigations.question:
Can we pull HRA datasets/knowledge via the live CCF API (reference organs,
cell-type terms, anatomical-structure terms) and link glucose-regulation
BioModels to HRA anatomy (Uberon organs) via a transparent biomodel
Digital Object + organ->models index?
investigations.hypothesis:
The HRA CCF API's reference-organs, cell-type-term-occurences, and
ontology-term-occurences endpoints are stable enough to drive a Step-based
fetch inside a process-bigraph composite; and simple synonym matching over
BioModels names against the HRA reference-organ set is enough to annotate a
useful fraction of glucose-regulation models with an Uberon organ, giving a
working organ->models index without a heavyweight NLP classifier.
Confirmed: live runs loaded 81 reference organs (69/81 Uberon-keyed),
149 Cell Ontology terms, and 288 anatomical-structure terms; synonym
matching over 25 "glucose regulation" search hits tagged 5/25 (20%) with
an HRA organ — 4 pancreas, 1 liver — a real but recall-limited (name-only)
organ->models index, not a complete one.
